subject: an English woman in her thirties of the Regency era with dark curly hair partly under a plain white muslin cap, bright observant eyes and a quick half-smile, wearing a simple high-waisted long-sleeved muslin gown and a soft shawl

panels.01-rectory: a lively English girl of about eleven in a simple 1780s cotton frock and cap, sitting on a window seat in a country rectory study lined with book-filled shelves, writing a story in a small notebook while her older sister paints a tiny portrait beside her, a clergyman father reading at his desk, warm afternoon light, Hampshire 1787
panels.02-refused: a young English woman of the 1790s in a plain muslin gown, standing in a rectory hallway holding a bundled manuscript tied with string, her elderly clergyman father in black coat and white neckcloth reading a short letter with a sympathetic expression, rain on the window, quiet disappointment and resolve, 1797
panels.03-bath: {S} walking with her mother and sister along a long curved terrace of honey-coloured Georgian stone houses in Bath in 1801, ladies in bonnets and pelisses, sedan chairs and carriages, the women looking back at their luggage, wide establishing view, a little wistful
panels.04-chawton: three women in Regency bonnets and shawls arriving by carriage at a modest red-brick cottage at a crossroads in the English village of Chawton in July 1809, a cottage garden, a gentleman brother helping unload trunks, summer light, a hopeful new start
panels.05-sittingroom: {S} writing at a very small round table in a shared cottage sitting room, using small sheets of paper and a quill, ready to slip a sheet under blotting paper, other women sewing by the fire, a swing door in the background just beginning to open, morning light through a sash window, quiet concentration and a hint of humour, 1811
panels.06-readaloud: {S} reading aloud from a new three-volume printed novel to her elderly mother and a lady visitor by candlelight in a cottage parlour in January 1813, the listeners amused and absorbed, a winter evening, warm and witty mood
panels.07-ending: {S} at a writing desk by a window in summer 1816, pages of a handwritten manuscript spread around her, some crossed through, writing a new chapter with fresh determination, a garden and village lane beyond the window, focused and thoughtful
panels.08-winchester: the quiet street outside a modest Georgian house in Winchester in 1817, the great medieval cathedral rising beyond the rooftops, a woman in a dark shawl standing at an upstairs window looking out at evening light, calm, gentle and dignified, no illness shown
